children: GE HealthCare (

) today announced a global clinical evaluation program spanning three continents and five internationally recognized institutions to assess StarGuide™ GX,i its next-generation digital 4D SPECT/CT system. Participating institutions include Hadassah Medical Center in Israel; Mayo Clinic in the United States; Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse in France; Peking University First Hospital in China; and Rambam Health Care Campus.

Across the program, participating institutions will evaluate image quality, quantitative performance, dynamic imaging and workflow while providing clinical and research feedback to help inform the future evolution of StarGuide GX.

“Nuclear medicine is entering a new era in which imaging is expected to do more than identify disease – it is increasingly being used to quantify biological processes, support treatment decisions and monitor response to therapy,” said Erez Levy, Executive Director, Molecular Imaging, GE HealthCare. “By working across multiple regions and care environments, we aim to generate clinical and research insights that can help inform innovation as imaging, quantitation and workflow needs evolve.”
Expanding quantitative and dynamic imaging capabilities

StarGuide GX uses dual-sided cadmium zinc telluride (dsCZT) detector technology and is designed to support high-sensitivity, high-resolution imaging, quantitative imaging and dynamic acquisitions. Its detector configuration allows the detectors to move close to the patient during imaging, while its patented dual-collimator detector design is intended to eliminate the need for manual external collimator exchanges and streamline imaging workflows.

Additionally, the system is engineered to support radionuclides across a broad energy range and, in research settings, it may also be evaluated for imaging radionuclides associated with emerging alpha-emitter research, including Actinium-225, focused on the potential to expand theranostic applications.ii

“The technological innovations introduced by StarGuide GX are particularly exciting for the future of theranostics,” shared Prof. Frederic Courbon, Head of the Imaging Department, Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse. “The system's ergonomic design and flexibility have the potential to significantly improve workflow while supporting precision in quantitative imaging and high-energy radionuclide applications. Our first experience suggests that StarGuide GX represents a meaningful step forward in enabling advanced theranostic practices.”

StarGuide GX also uses NVIDIA RTX™ accelerated computing to support image reconstruction, and includes a Low-Medium Energy collimator that is designed to provide up to 2.67-times system volume sensitivity.iii
Global collaborations advance nuclear medicine research
Five new, global clinical collaborations will evaluate the platform across diverse care settings:iv
Hadassah Medical Center (Israel): Evaluate advanced quantitative capabilities following the system’s recent field upgrade.
Mayo Clinic (United States): Evaluate advanced quantitative and dynamic imaging applications.

Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse (France): Assess StarGuide GX, the department's general-purpose SPECT/CT platform, across routine oncology imaging and clinical research.
Peking University First Hospital (China): Explore novel tracer research and preclinical applications.
Rambam Health Care Campus (Israel): Evaluate StarGuide GX imaging workflows through extensive clinical use across a broad range of nuclear medicine applications and tracers.

These new collaborations build on GE HealthCare’s work with University Hospital Essen in Germany, which in June 2026 opened a new state-of-the-art Nuclear Medicine Center featuring the world’s first installation of StarGuide GX SPECT/CT.
To date, these diverse healthcare institutions have scanned more than 1,000 patients.

StarGuide GX received CE Mark in November 2025 and is available for sale in select European Union member states. The system is 510(k) pending with the U.S. FDA and is not currently available for sale in the United States.

For more information about GE HealthCare’s molecular imaging portfolio, visit gehealthcare.com or see the system in the company’s booth at the European Association of Nuclear Medicine’s 2026 Annual Meeting, October 17-21 in Vienna, Austria.
